title: A/P Summary: the PDF and CSV match the rows and order on screen
custom_preconds:
Setup file (for Claude sessions; a tester does not need it)

Preconditions

  • You are signed in as a user with the "Admin" role, with {Location-A} as your current location.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919.
  • The organization has open documents in these reports at two locations, {Location-A} and {Location-B}, and you are enrolled at both; {Location-A}'s name comes first in A to Z order.
    For example: {Location-A} is Staging Heavy Duty - 9919 and {Location-B} is Staging Lethbridge - 4310.
  • Vendors {Vendor-A} and {Vendor-B} have open documents at both locations on today's date, at least two each, with different amounts.
    For example: {Vendor-A} is ZZAUTOTEST S3-06 Export One and {Vendor-B} is ZZAUTOTEST S3-06 Export Two.
  • Starting screen: Reports > Finance > A/P Summary is open in a desktop browser window 1440 px wide, as opened from the Reports menu, with the Vendor filter showing {Vendor-A} and {Vendor-B} ticked.
  • If any record above is missing, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
custom_steps:
1. Click the "Total" header once.
  2. Choose "Download (PDF)" from the ⋯ menu.
  3. Open the downloaded PDF and compare its rows with the screen, top to bottom.
  4. Choose "Download (CSV)" from the ⋯ menu.
  5. Open the CSV in a spreadsheet program and compare its rows with the screen.
  6. Without refreshing the page, click the the vendor name column (the first column) header.
  7. Choose "Download (CSV)" from the ⋯ menu again.
  8. Open the new CSV and compare its rows with the screen.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • Step 1: the rows sort by Total, largest first.
  • Step 2: the PDF downloads as a file and the "Success" message "Data exported successfully." shows.
  • Step 3: the PDF holds exactly the rows on screen for {Vendor-A} and {Vendor-B}, in the same order, and has a "Location" column, as the screen does (two locations are in view).
  • Step 4: the CSV downloads and the "Success" message "Data exported successfully." shows.
  • Step 5: the CSV holds exactly the same rows in the same order, with a "Location" column.
  • Step 6: the rows re-sort by name.
  • Step 7: the CSV downloads with the "Success" message.
  • Step 8: the new CSV follows the new on-screen order, by name, not the earlier Total order.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "A/R and A/P Report Sorting, Export and Location Filter", Confluence 947650561, version 5 (21 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 22 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11315, story SV-11533 (Story 3, Export to PDF and CSV), story SV-11536 (Story 6, Location column)

  • S3-R2: “The PDF downloads as a file.”
  • S3-R3: “The PDF and the CSV contain exactly the rows on screen for the chosen as-of date, customer or vendor and locations, in the on-screen sort, including a sort changed after an earlier export, without refreshing the page.”
  • S3-R6: “The Location column appears in the export under the same rule as on screen (Story 6).”
  • S3-R10: “A successful export shows the native "Success" message, "Data exported successfully." An export with no rows downloads nothing and shows the native warning "Empty export", "Export didn't yield any results".”
  • User Feedback Summary: “Export succeeds | "Success", "Data exported successfully." | Success toast, as on the other reports”
  • S6-R2: “The column is shown when two or more locations are ticked (All locations counts when the report's list has two or more) and hidden when one or none is ticked.”
